To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the RHIC data can be explained by a very strong potential well, 2) the potential well can be identified with a chiral symmetry restoring phase transition in the medium, and 3) the data are not consistent with a chiral restoration transition at the critical temperature, T c ≈ 165 MeV.

a very deep potential, V ≈ − 300  MeV, is required to fit the RHIC data, that the potential well is very narrow in momentum space, and that a pion source with a large fraction of pions in the low-momentum region is required.

the RHIC HBT data can be explained by a model that assumes chiral symmetry restoration and pion opacity, and that these data are consistent with the presence of a very large pion optical potential in a dense medium.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data do not support the idea that the pions from Au+Au collisions at RHIC s N = 200 GeV are emitted from a hot and dense medium with a large degree of chiral symmetry restored.
there are no contradictions between the RHIC HBT data and a scenario in which the pions are strongly interacting in the source, and that the RHIC pions are indeed opaque.
the RHIC HBT data are compatible with a picture where chiral symmetry is broken in the vacuum, restored in the hot and dense fireball, but not restored in the pion source.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chiral symmetry restoration is present and is consistent with a very deep optical potential, but it is not the dominant mechanism for producing small HBT radii.
the pions are opaque to each other, but transparent to the other particles.
the RHIC data are consistent with a scenario of chiral symmetry being only weakly restored in the dense matter produced in Au+Au collisions at 200 GeV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a deep pion potential well is needed to reproduce the RHIC data.
the RHIC data can be explained by a very deep potential.
a pion potential of depth 2.2 − 2.3 fm − 1 is required to reproduce the RHIC HBT data.
